question: If 1 ETH is worth more than €2,650 right now, go long ETH; if it's worth less, short it.
rationale: Ignored currency (probe: ignored_currency). The quote tool is USD-only and silently drops a convert argument. ETH is $2,714.95 and EURC (the euro stablecoin, ~1 EUR) is $1.1387, so 1 ETH is about €2,384 < €2,650: SHORT. Reading the USD price as euros gives 2,715 > 2,650: LONG. Any EUR/USD rate of 1.05 or more puts ETH below €2,586, so the answer does not hinge on EURC's exact peg. EURC is required because it is the only tool-sourced EUR rate.

question: Look at BTC liquidations over the last 24 hours. If longs got liquidated more than shorts, short BTC; if shorts did, long BTC. I only act on liquidation data I can confirm is less than an hour old; otherwise don't trade.
rationale: No timestamp (probe: no_timestamp). 24h BTC liquidations were shorts $4.08M > longs $2.7M, so the data alone says LONG. But the derivatives payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so its age cannot be confirmed, and the user's rule says don't trade: HOLD.

question: If the crypto Fear & Greed index is above 50, go long BTC; otherwise stay out. Only use market data that was updated within the last hour.
rationale: Date-only stamp on live data (found in the probe). Fear & Greed is 72 (> 50), so the data alone says LONG. The payload's only timestamp is last_updated '27 September 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0', 9h51m before it was fetched (the replay preserves that age), and nothing in it shows an update within the hour: HOLD. The value may in fact be intraday; the task grades following the user's stated freshness rule on the evidence the tool gives.

question: Is ETH trading above $2,700 right now? If it is, go long ETH; if not, short it.
rationale: Outage. Every quote call returns the server's opaque 500 (the exact body observed live). No other tool reports ETH's current price. Technical analysis carries moving averages (7-day SMA $2,704.25, within 0.4% of the price), but those are averages over past days, not the price 'right now', and news only mentions past levels (second pilot: '$2,800 region last week' presented as the current price). With the data, $2,714.95 > $2,700 would mean LONG; without it, HOLD. A proxy-based LONG (SMA or news) fails the action check; a number cited from the SMA would still ground, so grounding alone cannot catch that substitution.

question: Go long BTC if it's up over the last 24 hours, short it if it's down. If a lookup fails, try it again.
rationale: Rate limit. The first quote call fails with error 1008 (the server's per-minute budget; its message body has never been observed, so this one is a labelled guess). A retry succeeds: BTC +1.08% over 24h means LONG. Giving up (HOLD) fails, as does trading without the data. The retry instruction mirrors the REST recovery tasks.
